# Building

BlitzLLVM builds with CMake. The compiler is `blitzcc`, and it carries the runtime library with it. The first configure builds the dependencies (Vulkan headers, SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer, linked statically except for the AVIF, JPEG XL and WebP codecs of SDL3_image which are shared libraries, and the header-only VulkanMemoryAllocator) from the submodules in `third_party/`, which takes a few minutes.

## Requirements

* CMake 4.2 or newer.
* Git, for fetching the dependencies.
* A C++20 compiler: Visual Studio on Windows, Clang or GCC on Linux, Apple Clang on macOS.
* Ninja on Linux and macOS.
* NASM on x86 and x64, optional. It builds the assembly of dav1d (AVIF images). Without it the build still works, with a warning, and AVIF images decode more slowly. Pass `-DBLITZLLVM_REQUIRE_NASM=ON` to make a missing NASM an error, as the nightly builds do. Install it with `winget install nasm` on Windows, `sudo apt-get install nasm` on Debian and Ubuntu or `brew install nasm` on macOS. It is found on `PATH`, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\bin\NASM` or in `C:\Program Files\NASM`; set `BLITZLLVM_NASM` to its path if it is elsewhere.
* Python 3, optional. It enables the `suite-coverage` test.

### Windows

Install Visual Studio with the "Desktop development with C++" workload. The nightly builds use Visual Studio 18 2026; the repository also has presets for Visual Studio 17 2022 and for clang (see below).

### Linux

SDL3 needs the development packages of the windowing, audio and input libraries. On Debian and Ubuntu:

```sh
sudo apt-get install -y ninja-build libx11-dev libxext-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxrandr-dev \
  libxss-dev libxtst-dev libxfixes-dev libwayland-dev libxkbcommon-dev libdecor-0-dev \
  libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libudev-dev libdrm-dev libgbm-dev libegl-dev
```

### macOS

```sh
brew install ninja
```

## Getting the source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM.git
cd BlitzLLVM
git submodule update --init --depth 1 cmake third_party
```

The submodules in `cmake/` and `third_party/` are required to build. The `extra/` submodules only hold the original Blitz3D and BlitzPlus sources that the function test suite tools compare against, so they are not needed to build. Fetch them with `git submodule update --init extra` if you want them.

## Build

Linux and macOS:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
```

Windows:

```bat
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 18 2026" -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release
```

Instead of choosing the generator yourself you can use a preset from `CMakePresets.json`: `windows-x64-msvc2022` (Visual Studio 17 2022) or `windows-x64-llvm` (Ninja Multi-Config with the LLVM toolchain from `cmake/toolchains/llvm.cmake`).

```bat
cmake --preset windows-x64-msvc2022
cmake --build --preset windows-x64-msvc2022 --config Release
```

The compiler ends up in the build directory as `blitzcc` (`blitzcc.exe`), with the runtime in a `runtime` directory next to it (an install puts it in `lib/blitzllvm/runtime`).

### System libraries (Linux)

On Linux the dependencies can come from the distribution instead of the submodules, which keeps them out of the packages and lets the distribution update them. Each one has a cache variable that is `AUTO` (use the system's if `pkg-config` finds a new enough copy, otherwise build the submodule), `ON` (fail if there is none) or `OFF` (always build the submodule):

| Variable | Takes | How programs use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BLITZ_SYSTEM_SDL3` | SDL3 (3.4.0 or newer, `BLITZ_SDL3_MINIMUM_VERSION`) | linked as a shared library |
| `BLITZ_SYSTEM_SDL3_IMAGE`, `BLITZ_SYSTEM_SDL3_MIXER` | SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer (need the system's SDL3) | linked as shared libraries |
| `BLITZ_SYSTEM_IMAGE_CODECS` | libavif (with dav1d), libjxl and libwebp | loaded when a program opens such an image |
| `BLITZ_SYSTEM_AUDIO_CODECS` | opusfile (with libopus and libogg) | loaded when a program plays an Opus file |
| `BLITZ_SYSTEM_FFMPEG` | FFmpeg, but only if it is LGPL and has the decoders listed in `dependencies.cmake` | loaded when a program opens a movie |

The libraries that programs link to are written to `runtime/system-libraries.txt` next to the runtime, which `blitzcc` adds to the link. On Debian and Ubuntu the `.deb` depends on (or, for the libraries that are loaded when needed, recommends) the packages that own them, at least in the version that the package was built with. The distributions ship FFmpeg with GPL parts (check with `avcodec_license()`), so the bundled LGPL build is used there. Windows and macOS always build the submodules.

## Install

```sh
cmake --install build --config Release --prefix dist
```

This creates:

```
dist/bin/blitzcc          the compiler
dist/lib/blitzllvm/runtime/  the runtime libraries and sources, lib has to stay next to bin
dist/userlibs/            user libraries, with a README
```

## Tests

```sh
ctest --test-dir build -C Release
```

This compiles and runs every program in `tests/` and the function test suite in `tests/suite` without a window (`BLITZ_HEADLESS=1`). The function test suite, the audio test, the close prompt test and the AutoSuspend tests run twice: as the compiler builds by default (Release), and with `-d` (Debug, which implies `--profile`). The Debug ones have `debug` in their names, for example `suite-debug-run-math`; `ctest -R debug` runs only those. Tests that look at pixels need a window and a GPU and are skipped unless you configure with `-DBLITZ_TEST_GPU=ON`. The tests need `clang` (see [[Installation]]).

### Continuous integration

The `Test` workflow (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs the tests on Linux (all of them, or only the ones a change can affect, see below), for every pull request to `root` and for every push to `root`. It also runs the tests that need a window and a GPU (`-DBLITZ_TEST_GPU=ON`): the runners have no GPU, so Mesa's llvmpipe renders Vulkan on the CPU inside a virtual X server (`xvfb-run`). To run the same thing on your own Linux machine:

```sh
sudo apt-get install -y mesa-vulkan-drivers xvfb xdotool x11-utils
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBLITZ_TEST_GPU=ON
cmake --build build
cd build/code_compiler && xvfb-run -a ctest -j8 --output-on-failure
```

#### Which tests run

A pull request does not run the tests that its changes can not affect. The `changes` job of the workflow compares the pull request with `root`, `.github/scripts/test-select.py` maps every changed file to the parts it can affect (the rules are in `tests/test_selection.json`), and `Test (Linux)` runs only the tests of those parts, plus the few that are not in any part (`lex-test`, `suite-coverage`, `ci-test-select`, `ci-test-report`). The tests that were left out show as skipped (⏭️) in the test comment, with the reason. A skipped test counts as passed, so the required check stays green.

| What changed | What runs |
| --- | --- |
| Documentation, the wiki sources, `extra/`, the benchmarks, other workflows | Nothing. The check succeeds without building. |
| One part of the runtime, for example `sound.c` (audio), `network.c` (network), `movie.cpp` (movies), `gui_*.cpp` (BlitzPlus GUI), `scene*.cpp` (Blitz3D), `files.c` (files), `graphics_*.cpp` (everything that draws) | The tests of that part, in Release and Debug. |
| A test program (`tests/suite/x.bb`) | The compile and run tests of that program only. |
| A test of one tool or the command line (`tests/cli`, `tests/format`, `tests/tidy`, `code_format`, `code_tidy`, `code_tools`) | The tests of that tool. |
| The compiler, the core of the runtime, the CMake files, `third_party`, the workflow, the test selection itself, or any file that has no rule | Everything. |

Everything also runs for every push to `root`, for a manual run, and for a pull request with the label `run-all-tests` (add the label, then re-run the workflow; the label is read when the run starts). The push to `root` is the safety net: if a rule skips something it should not have, the run on `root` finds it.

To change the rules, edit `tests/test_selection.json`: `areas` says which tests (by name) belong to a part, `rules` says which parts a changed file affects (the first rule that matches wins; `"all"` runs everything, `"none"` nothing, `[]` only the tests that are in no part). When in doubt, map a file to more parts, not fewer. `python3 tests/ci/test_select.py` tests the rules (it also runs as the ctest test `ci-test-select`), and it fails if a program in `tests/suite` is in no part. To see what a change would run, put the changed files in a file and run `python3 .github/scripts/test-select.py changes --changed files.txt`.

#### Requiring the tests before a pull request can be merged

The check is named **Test (Linux)**. A workflow on its own never blocks a merge; GitHub only blocks it for checks that the repository marks as *required*. This is a repository setting, so the maintainer has to make it (it can not be part of a pull request).

1. Merge the pull request that adds `test.yml`, and let it run once on `root` (or on any pull request). GitHub only offers a check in the list below after it has run in the repository during the last 7 days.
2. Open the repository on GitHub, then **Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New ruleset → New branch ruleset**. (The older way is **Settings → Branches → Add branch protection rule** with the branch name pattern `root`; the steps below are the same.)
3. Give it a name such as `root`, set **Enforcement status** to **Active**, and under **Target branches** choose **Add target → Include by pattern** and enter `root`.
4. Under **Branch rules** tick **Require a pull request before merging**, and **Require status checks to pass**.
5. In **Require status checks to pass**, tick **Require branches to be up to date before merging** if a pull request has to be tested on top of the current `root` (recommended), then **Add checks**, search for `Test (Linux)` and select it. Do the same for the three `build (...)` checks of the Pull Request workflow if the builds should be required as well. Leave the source on **Any source**, or pick **GitHub Actions**.
6. **Create**. The merge button of a pull request is now disabled until `Test (Linux)` is green, and pushes straight to `root` are refused too (unless the ruleset lists a bypass for administrators).

Things to know:

* The check must always report. `test.yml` therefore has no `paths` filter (the selection above is done inside the job); a required check that is skipped never turns green and blocks the pull request forever.
* If you rename the job (`name:` in `test.yml`) you have to change the required check in the ruleset too, or every pull request waits for a check that no longer exists.
* The name has to be unique among the workflows. A job called `Test (Linux)` in two workflows would be ambiguous.
* With **Require branches to be up to date** a pull request has to be updated with `root` after every other merge. Without it, a pull request can be merged green while being broken by a newer commit on `root`.
* Pushes to `root` run the tests too, so a break that slipped in (for example by an administrator bypass) shows up on the commit.
